jobs.desc:
Porch Group is a leading vertical software and insurance platform and is positioned to be the best partner to help homebuyers move, maintain, and fully protect their homes. We offer differentiated products and services, with homeowners insurance at the center of this relationship. We differentiate and look to win in the massive and growing homeowners insurance opportunity by 1) providing the best services for homebuyers, 2) led by advantaged underwriting in insurance, 3) to protect the whole home.

As a leader in the home services software-as-a-service (“SaaS”) space, we’ve built deep relationships with approximately 30 thousand companies that are key to the home-buying transaction, such as home inspectors, mortgage companies, and title companies.

In 2020, Porch Group rang the Nasdaq bell and began trading under the ticker symbol PRCH. We are looking to build a truly great company and are JUST GETTING STARTED.

**Job Title:** Product Manager, AI-Native Prototyping

**Location:** United States

**Workplace Type:** Remote

**Job Summary**
---------------

The future is bright for the Porch Group, and we’d love for you to be a part of it as our **Product Manager, AI-Native Prototyping** .

As a Product Manager, AI-Native Prototyping, you will own strategy, discovery, and user experience for your assigned product areas. This is a hands-on role focused on identifying customer problems, setting priorities, designing solutions, and partnering with engineering to deliver measurable results. You will independently create initial workflows and functional prototypes using AI tools such as Claude Design and Claude Code, then validate them directly with customers before engineering builds the production version. Design and prototyping ownership are core expectations of the role, with specialist support when available. Working within the vision set by the Head of Product and alongside an Associate Product Manager and delivery team, you will help ensure Porch builds the right things for the customers we serve.

  

**What You Will Do As A Product Manager, AI-Native Prototyping**
----------------------------------------------------------------

* Own product strategy and the roadmap for your assigned product areas, within the vision and priorities set by the Head of Product.

* Prioritize opportunities using customer evidence, business impact, effort, and strategic alignment, and clearly explain your decisions and trade-offs.

* Lead customer discovery through interviews, feedback channels (Intercom, Canny, NPS), Sales and Customer Success input, product data, and competitive research, validating problems and assumptions before committing engineering resources.

* Independently design user flows and build interactive, functional prototypes with AI tools such as Claude Design and Claude Code, then test complete workflows with customers and iterate based on their feedback.

* Define feature requirements, expected behaviors, scope, and success metrics, make product decisions during development, and review delivered features against the intended customer problem.

* Apply established design patterns, accessibility considerations, and consistent product experiences.

* Partner with the Associate Product Manager (APM) and delivery team to turn validated solutions into development-ready work. You own priorities, scope, and product acceptance, while the APM coordinates Jira, sprints, and releases.

* Measure adoption, engagement, and customer outcomes after launch, and use the results to improve the product and adjust priorities.

Use AI to accelerate research, design, and prototyping, and identify customer-facing AI opportunities that solve meaningful problems.  

  

**What You Will Bring As A Product Manager, AI-Native Prototyping**
-------------------------------------------------------------------

* Product Ownership: 3 or more years of product management experience, preferably in B2B SaaS. Demonstrated ownership, judgment, and results matter

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We believe powerful AI can compress a century of scientific progress into a decade. Claude Science is a big part of building toward that future.

Claude Science is an AI workbench that gives researchers a single environment for work that today spans dozens of disconnected tools — literature, specialized databases, scientific computing, analysis, and publication-ready outputs. Claude Science already renders protein structures, genome tracks, and chemical structures natively, and coordinates multi-agent workflows with built-in review for citation and calculation errors — and we're just getting started. Much of this is being built 0→1 right now, in a category no one has defined yet.

We're growing the Claude Science product team. As a Product Manager on Claude Science, you will own a major area of the roadmap end to end — think expanding into new scientific fields, landing new model capabilities with researchers, or making the workbench ready for enterprise R&D teams — and help shape the overall product direction alongside the rest of the team. You'll spend real time with researchers in academic labs, biotech and pharma R&D, and research institutes to understand how science actually gets done — from hypothesis to analysis to publication and beyond— and turn what you learn into shipped product. You'll partner directly with our research teams to make the models better at science, help decide which fields and workflows we go after next, and shape what it takes for Claude Science to be trusted in enterprise and regulated research environments.

We're looking for experienced product managers and founders with real scientific or technical depth: people who can hold their own in a conversation with a structural biologist or a computational chemist, get in the weeds of model transcripts and evals, and still zoom out to help define a product category. You thrive in ambiguity, uncover non-obvious use cases for nascent capabilities, and bring those insights back to research.

Our north star is for Claude Science to accelerate scientific progress — across biology, chemistry, physics, and beyond — from early discovery through real-world application, by an order of magnitude.

jobs.title: Product Manager I
jobs.desc:
**Our Mission**
---------------

As the world’s number 1 job site\*, our mission is to help people get jobs. We strive to cultivate an inclusive and accessible workplace where all people feel comfortable being themselves. We're looking to grow our teams with more people who share our enthusiasm for innovation and creating the best experience for job seekers.

(\*Comscore, Total Visits, March 2026)

**Day to Day**
--------------

You'll own capabilities at the foundation of how the company moves, stores, and reasons about data: collecting analytical events in real time and batch, housing them cost-efficiently across thousands of datasets, and making them queryable at massive scale. Your focus is building paved paths, opinionated end-to-end workflows, that let teams produce trusted data outcomes without stitching together systems, filing tickets, or becoming amateur platform engineers. You'll be accountable for the full user-facing capability across whatever products it touches, absorbing the friction from start to finish. You'll build these paths alongside your customers, working with engineers on the technical design and with internal users, so decisions rest on real use cases and direct feedback. Expect to stay hands-on: tracing how data flows end-to-end, finding where paths break down, and shifting more of the work from procedural steps to simple, declarative intent.

Making the platform AI-ready is core to the role. You'll shape how data is exposed to AI systems and agents through natural-language access, programmatic access, and AI-assisted analysis, and you'll hold those capabilities to the same governance, quality, and observability bar as everything else. You're also expected to use AI fluently in your own work: speeding up discovery and analysis, prototyping and pressure-testing ideas, drafting specs, synthesizing customer feedback, and automating workflows so you spend more time on the product strategy.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Partner with engineering teams and other interested parties to prioritize and manage roadmaps for delivering toward product vision incrementally and efficiently.
* Communicate roadmap and product plan to and get alignment with leadership, collaborators and interested parties.
* Be the face of the customer internally, advocating for, and representing their needs, opportunities, and product requirements.
* Identify, and monitor product goals and success metrics.
* Iterate quickly to launch new features and make data-driven judgments to test their efficacy.
* Provide clear written and verbal updates on the roadmap and progress toward goals to leadership and collaborators.

We're looking for an Associate Product Manager to be Rezdy's dependable NA presence — covering the hours our Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team aren't online. This is a strong fit for someone energized by operational rigor and real-time problem-solving: comfortable triaging under pressure, translating between technical and commercial audiences, and building product judgment by working closely alongside a senior PM rather than owning a roadmap from day one. Pacific timezone

**What you'll do:**

* Connect the time zones. Be the dependable daily link between North America stakeholders — support and account management teams — and the Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team, flagging decisions and blockers in real time rather than letting them wait for the next overlap window.
* Be the NA distribution conduit for Commercial leads and distribution partners (Viator, GYG, etc) and Distribution Resellers
* Keep incidents moving and visible during NA hours. Triage escalations that occur in NA working hours against a defined severity framework, looping in the senior PM and dev lead when judgment calls exceed current scope, and making sure NA support and AM teams get clear, live updates rather than waiting for the next AU working day.
* Surface and track AM churn risk. Own intake of NA account-manager-flagged churn risk — capturing impact and urgency the moment it's raised — so it's framed and ready to compete fairly when the senior PM and dev lead plan the sprint.
* Answer for what's in flight. Be NA's go-to for "is this expected / is this known / what's the status" questions on Booking Manager and Distribution, working from close sync with the senior PM's roadmap and known-issues context rather than independent authority over it.
* Share release communication in NA hours. Help execute the existing release process — communication and post-release follow-up specifically during NA hours — rather than owning release planning or prioritization.
* Partner with Engineering at a working level. Build enough fluency in our data architecture to relay NA-side context accurately to engineering, without owning technical trade-off decisions.
* Put AI tools to work. Use AI tools to speed up research, troubleshooting, and day-to-day tasks — a lever for moving faster, not a replacement for judgment.

**What you'll bring:**

* 2+ years of experience in product management, product operations, or a closely related operational/customer-facing role, ideally in B2B SaaS.
* Comfort working within another PM's priorities and roadmap — bringing your own judgment and context to how that work gets executed
* Experience with incident or issue management processes, and communicating through them clearly under time pressure.
* Comfort working with legacy technology systems and the teams that maintain them — able to translate between legacy constraints and current product priorities for both engineering and commercial audiences.
* Strong written communication skills — able to adjust tone and depth for audiences ranging from support and account management teams to engineering.
* Ease operating in process-driven environments (Jira, Slack, or equivalent).
* Comfort picking up domain concepts across different product types — e.g., transactional booking flows versus distribution/channel connectivity — without needing deep expertise in both on day one.

**Nice to have:**

* Experience in the travel, tours, or activities booking software space.
* Familiarity with multi-brand or multi-product portfolios (Expedition Software operates Checkfront, Rezdy, and Regiondo).
* Prior experience in a support, account management, or customer-facing product role.

The salary range for this position is $80,000-$95,000, commensurate with years of experience, skillset, and qualifications.

# Associate Product Manager, AI Agents Implementation (Brooklyn)

Location:Flatbush, NYCompany:AUI™

## Description:

**About AUI**

AUI builds Apollo, a neurosymbolic foundation model for AI agents that do consequential work, where accuracy, reliability, and visibility matter — conversations with customers, and the processes behind them. Instead of describing behavior in a prompt and hoping the model complies, Apollo compiles declared rules into a checkable program. Constraints are enforced by the system rather than requested of the model, so “this agent will never do X” is something you verify, not something you hope for. The language model works as a translation layer at either end — structuring what a person (or another agent, or a system) says into symbolic slots on the way in, and generating fluent responses on the way out.

That guarantee is what LLMs structurally can never achieve. We serve companies from startups to the Fortune 500, across regulated industries, retail, and travel — environments where an agent that improvises is a liability, and where someone has to answer for every action it takes.

Apollo-1 is a self-serve platform, and most teams can build on it themselves. Large enterprises — with deeper integrations and more involved internal processes — can use a hand getting their agents all the way to production. Our commercial team also needs proof-of-concept agents built for prospects, fast. That’s this team.

**The role**

You’re joining our deployment team, serving two constituencies.

**Internal.** Our product and commercial teams need working agents — proofs of concept for prospects, reference builds, agents that pressure-test the platform before customers find its edges. You’ll build them, often on short notice, often for a business you learned about today.

**External.** The most complex enterprise deployments, where the agent has to hold a real company’s rules across hundreds of scenarios and act on live systems. You’ll be in the room with their operators and subject-matter experts, not reading a requirements doc someone else wrote.

An agent starts life as a real business: a bank’s dispute policy, an airline’s rebooking rules, a retailer’s returns matrix. Someone has to sit inside that mess, understand how the business actually works, and turn it into a program the platform can enforce and certify. Then train it, grade it, try to break it, and sign off that it’s ready to act on a customer’s behalf.

The loop closes back into the product. What you solve by hand for one enterprise should become something the next customer can do themselves, and you’ll be one of the loudest sources of truth about what the platform can’t do automatically.

**What you’ll do**

- Sit with partner teams to extract how their business actually operates — including the rules nobody wrote down and the exceptions everyone knows about
- Author agent programs: translate policy, process, and edge cases into structured, unambiguous declarations the platform can enforce
- Run training rounds — design scenarios, simulate conversations, grade outputs, and iterate until behavior holds
- Own certification: prove a program does what it claims before it ships, and triage it when it regresses
- Find the contradictions. Real businesses run on rules that conflict. You’ll be the one who notices the refund window doesn’t square with the cancellation clause, and who drives the decision on which one wins
- Build proofs of concept alongside our commercial team, and support technical discovery with large prospects — you’re the person in the room who can answer “can it really do that?”

- Support validation and quality activities, including data review and cleanup, in partnership with Laboratory, Quality, and Regulatory teams.

**About CodeHS**
----------------

CodeHS is a comprehensive platform helping K-12 schools teach computer science. We provide curriculum, professional development, and a full software platform. CodeHS is used by millions of students and thousands of schools and districts around the US and the world.

**Mission**
-----------

**The mission of CodeHS is to empower all students to meaningfully impact the future.** We believe that in the 21st century, coding is a foundational skill, just like reading and writing. That’s why we say: **Read, Write, Code.** Coding and computer science are essential skills for students to learn and schools to teach.

### **Location**

**Chicago — our River North office, five days a week.** Reports to Zach Galant, CTO & co-founder.

CodeHS is hybrid overall. We have people in other offices and people who work remotely, and you’ll work with them regularly. This role is in person because it depends on coming up to speed quickly — on the product, on our customers, and on how the engineering team works — and that happens faster sitting next to people. So does mentorship. We want someone who wants to work that way and is excited about getting to work in person in the office.

We are growing our product team within engineering

We have about fifteen engineers in small project teams that re-form each cycle, and we ship constantly. What limits our impact usually isn’t engineering capacity — it’s conviction about what to build, why, and how to communicate it to the rest of the team and our customers. We want someone who can get that conviction from teachers, districts, the market, our data, and our own team, and turn it into something engineering can act on.

### **The role**

This role is for someone earlier in their career who wants to learn product management by doing it.

You’ll own projects within a product area, from understanding the problem through launch and adoption. You’ll make the calls on scope, specs, and tradeoffs for your projects and work closely with the engineers building them. The bigger calls — which problems to take on, and what not to build — we’ll make together at first, and more of them become yours as you show judgment.

You’ll sit in on the conversations where we set priorities across teams, so you can see how those decisions get made.

### **How you work**

**You build.** When you have an idea, go make a version of it. Not production code — a working prototype you drove an AI coding agent to build. Engineers review and take it to completion.

**You write things down.** Specs, product briefs, the reasoning behind a decision. If it isn’t written down here, it doesn’t count.

**You talk to the people who use this.** Much of the work is strategy and synthesis. But when the answer is in a classroom or on a call with a district, you go. It isn’t a heavy travel role, but you will need to join calls, talk to people on the team and customers, and build an understanding beyond just reasoning through things on your own.

**You connect engineering to everyone else.** Sales, customer success, support, and curriculum all have product or tooling needs. Your job is to gather the information, synthesize it, and use that to inform what the right things are to build.

### **You should be**

**Early in your career, with real work behind you.** At least a year of full-time work experience, in any role. A product management internship counts too. You don’t need to have been a PM.

**Comfortable around code,** without necessarily having been an engineer. You can read a pull request and ask an engineer good questions about how something works and what it would take to change.

**Fluent with AI, and adaptive to how things are changing.** You use AI to guide your thinking and move quickly, but you don’t hide behind it for judgment. jobs.title: Associate Product Manager
jobs.desc:
*Copart, Inc. a technology leader and the premier online vehicle auction platform globally, with over 200 facilities located across the world, Copart links vehicle sellers to more than 750,000 buyers in over 190 countries. We believe in providing an unmatched experience, every day and everywhere, driven by our people, processes, and technology.*

**Associate Product Manager**

**Location:** San Francisco, CA (in office)

**Reports to:** Product Management Leader

**Classification:** Full-Time

**Travel:** To operating locations, Dallas headquarters, and customers as needed

**About Copart**

Copart is a global leader in online vehicle auctions and automotive remarketing services. We serve Members across multiple countries through a culture built on integrity, ownership, innovation, operational excellence, and results.

**The Opportunity**

The Associate Product Manager will support product discovery and delivery while building the foundational skills required to lead Copart products.

This role will combine customer empathy, commercial judgment, data-informed decision-making, and hands-on execution to advance early-career product management. The successful candidate will operate effectively in a fast-moving environment, work across functions and geographies, and turn complex needs into simple, scalable solutions.

**What You Will Do**

**Product Strategy and Customer Insight**

* Define a clear product vision and roadmap for early-career product management.
* Develop a deep understanding of buyer, seller, partner, employee, and operational needs through research, data, and direct observation.
* Translate enterprise priorities into measurable customer and business outcomes.
* Make explicit tradeoffs based on value, effort, risk, and strategic fit.

**Execution and Delivery**

* Partner with Engineering, Design, Data, Operations, Marketing, Legal, Security, and other teams to deliver high-quality solutions.
* Write clear product requirements, define acceptance criteria, and maintain an actionable backlog.
* Establish release plans, manage dependencies, and remove barriers to execution.
* Ensure solutions are secure, scalable, reliable, accessible, and supportable.

**Measurement and Continuous Improvement**

* Use qualitative and quantitative evidence to evaluate product performance and prioritize improvements.
* Run structured experiments and convert learning into roadmap decisions.
* Communicate progress, risks, decisions, and results with clarity.

**Collaboration and Change Leadership**

* Build trust with field and corporate stakeholders and engage users early throughout discovery and delivery.
* Create practical adoption plans, training, communications, and feedback loops.
* Model ownership, disciplined decision-making, and follow-through.
* Represent the product perspective in cross-functional planning and executive discussions.

**What You Bring**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience; internship or project experience in product, analytics, design, engineering, or operations preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to define ambiguous problems, align stakeholders, and deliver measurable outcomes.
* Strong analytical, communication, prioritization, and decision-making skills.
* Experience partnering across Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Operations, and business functions.
* Familiarity with agile product development, experimentation, analytics, and modern cloud platforms.
* Ability to work from Copart’s San Francisco office and travel to operating locations, Dallas headquarters, and customers as needed.

**How Success Will Be Measured**

* Establish a clear strategy, roadmap, and measurable outcomes for early-career product management.
* Build strong alignment with Product, Technology, Operations, and Business Leadership.
* Deliver priority capabilities with high quality and disciplined execution.
* Improve customer or employee experience, adoption, efficiency, revenue, risk, or other agreed product outcom

**The Fitch Solutions Product organization is currently seeking a Product Owner based in our NYC office to join the Scoring & Risk Analytics Tribe.**

With teams operating in over 30 countries, our analysts, lawyers, journalists and economists combine global perspective with deep local expertise. We pair human intelligence with innovative technology to deliver high-quality credit research, data and proprietary analytics that help global markets manage risk and identify opportunity. Our success is powered by an inclusive, collaborative culture in which every expert voice contributes to exceptional client value.

Fitch Solutions is a part of Fitch Group, wholly owned by the Hearst Corporation, which is comprised of three main businesses: Fitch Ratings | Fitch Solutions | Fitch Learning.

The Fitch Solutions Product organization is organized into five product tribes, each with a single lead, roadmap and defined scope. The Product Owner will sit within the **Scoring & Risk Analytics Tribe**, which is responsible for the model-based outputs across Fitch Solutions’ portfolio and in the development and governance of its various credit risk assessment tools and capabilities.

This role involves working closely with the Product Manager and cross-functional teams to drive the product lifecycle from ideation to launch. * Agile Ceremonies: Run agile ceremonies, including backlog grooming, sprint planning, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.

* Customer Interaction: Discuss features with customers, focusing on usability, time to value, feature completeness, and the overall user journey.
* Prototyping and Testing: Collaborate with engineering and design to prototype features, conduct A/B testing, and validate designs with end users.
* Issue Resolution: Handle issues with current features and provide solutions based on customer feedback.
* Performance Monitoring: Track and analyze product performance metrics e.g. team productivity, product adoption, feature performance. This role would focus on collection, analysis, and reporting as well as implementing improvements at the squad level.

### **Minimum qualifications:**

**About the job**
-----------------

At YouTube, we believe that everyone deserves to have a voice, and that the world is a better place when we listen, share, and build community through our stories. We work together to give everyone the power to share their story, explore what they love, and connect with one another in the process. We explore new ideas, solve real problems, and have fun – and we do it all together.

As a Product Manager on the YouTube Premium team, you will build the experiences that make Premium worth it every day for members. You will guide products from conception to launch by connecting the technical and business worlds. You will own a portfolio of Premium features, from improving core functionality to launching differentiated capabilities that deepen engagement.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

jobs.title: Associate Product Manager
jobs.desc:
**About Us**

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

**The Role**

Our Product Managers operate like owners of their surface. The APM role is how we develop the next ones.

You join a senior PM's team and own a defined part of a banking product. You ship to real customers in your first quarter. You get real scope, a direct mentor, and honest feedback every week. The goal: in 18 months, you own a surface as a full PM.

In banking, every interaction carries trust. Money moves, cards get declined, payments settle or fail. You learn how a regulated financial product works from the inside, and you learn to build products that customers trust with their money.

**What You'll Do**

**Own a feature area end to end.** Your mentor gives you a defined part of the product. You own it from the problem to the result. Frame the problem, write the spec, ship it, and measure what changed. When the data shows a better direction, bring a recommendation, not only the data.

**Build with Design and Engineering every day.** Sit with your designer and engineers from the first sketch to the launch. Write specs that engineers want to read. Give clear feedback on flows and edge cases, because in banking an edge case is a customer's money. Unblock the team fast, and run launches end to end. In a regulated product, this also means that you bring Compliance and Operations in early, so they do not block the launch late.

**Get close to customers.** Talk to founders and finance teams every week. Read support tickets. Learn how early-stage companies think about cash, spend, and risk, and bring that knowledge back to the team.

**Decide with data.** Define success before you build. Pull your own data. Report clearly what worked and what did not.

**Build with AI.** Use frontier models to test ideas, build prototypes, analyze customer feedback, and draft specs. We expect AI to make you faster, and we expect you to find new ways to use it for our customers.

### **What You Get**

* A named senior PM as your mentor, and a defined scope from your first week.
* Weekly 1:1s and structured reviews at 6 and 12 months.
* Direct exposure to product reviews with leadership.
* A clear path to Product Manager.

**Who You Are**

* Based in NYC
* You have 1 – 3 years of experience in product, engineering, data, consulting, banking, at a startup, or in a customer facing role. Or you started something of your own.
* You are analytical. You are comfortable with SQL, spreadsheets, and numbers, and you check your own work.
* You are curious about how money moves. Knowledge of ACH, card networks, KYC/KYB, or reconciliation is a plus. We teach the rest.
* You use AI every day, and you can show us something you built with it.
* You write clearly. You can explain a complex problem in one page.
* You take feedback well and act on it fast.
* You take ownership. When something is broken, you fix it or you find the person who can.

**Nice to have:** a technical background or coding experience, work at a bank or fintech, or startup experience.

Our people are our most valuable asset. **Our target compensation range for this role is $133K - $160K.** Compensation will be determined by leveling and performance throughout the interview process. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.
